transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Study of Olomorasib (LY3537982) in Combination With Standard of Care in Participants With Resected or Unresectable KRAS G12C-mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". Your earlier answers already covered 4 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. For this study, you need to have had chemotherapy and immunotherapy before surgery, and still have tumor cells found in the tissue after the operation. Did your surgery show that some tumor cells were still present?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had any surgery for this cancer. I was told it had spread too far for that to be an option, so I've only had systemic treatments like chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. Since you haven't had surgery, could you tell me if your cancer is considered Clinical Stage III and unresectable? Also, has your cancer progressed since you finished your platinum-based chemoradiotherapy?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if it's classified as Stage III, but I do know it's unresectable because it spread to my bones and lymph nodes. I haven't had chemoradiotherapy, only chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know the result of your PD-L1 test, which measures how much PD-L1 protein is on your cancer cells? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: That's something I'd need to ask about. I don't have that result on hand.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to swallow pills or capsules for your medication?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am able to swallow pills and capsules without any trouble.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any blood tests or lab work done in the last 2 weeks to check your blood counts and organ function?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the exact timing of my last blood tests, but I do know I'm currently being treated for lung inflammation from the Keytruda, so I've likely had recent labs done as part of that care.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your recent blood tests showed that your blood counts and organ function are within the normal range needed for this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm afraid I genuinely don't know. I haven't seen the specific results of those recent blood tests to know if they meet the study's requirements.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently use any form of birth control or contraception?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not pregnant or breastfeeding, so I don't use birth control for that reason.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be clear, are you currently using any method to prevent pregnancy, such as condoms, pills, or an IUD?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't use any birth control methods. I'm 63 and post-menopausal, so pregnancy isn't a concern for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told that your cancer has known changes in the EGFR or ALK genes? These are specific genetic markers in the tumor. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: They tested for EGFR I think, but I never heard the result. As for ALK, that's something I'd need to ask about.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received a specific result stating that your tumor has an EGFR or ALK mutation? If you don't have that report, would you be willing to ask your doctor for it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have a specific result stating that, because I never heard the outcome of the EGFR test. I'd need to ask my doctor about that to be sure.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any other type of cancer that was growing or needed active treatment in the last 2 years?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, this is the only cancer I've had.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a severe (Grade 3 or higher) immune-related side effect or allergic reaction from an immunotherapy medicine, or any immune-related side effect that is still ongoing?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am currently being treated for pneumonitis, which is lung inflammation caused by the Keytruda. It's an ongoing immune-related side effect that I'm managing with steroids right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
